references.text: Jesus says that whoever denies him before men, he will deny before his Father in heaven – parallel to being ashamed of Jesus and his words.

Direct parallel text in the Gospel of Mark: whoever is ashamed of Jesus and his words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will be ashamed of when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.
Matthew's parallel about the coming of the Son of Man in his Father's glory with his angels, when he will repay each according to their deeds.
Paul urges Timothy not to be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord – the same theme of not being ashamed of Jesus and the gospel.
Paul declares that he is not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God for salvation – the counterpart to not being ashamed of Jesus and his words.
Jesus says that whoever confesses him before men, the Son of Man will confess before the angels of God, and whoever denies him will be denied – a closely related theme.
Daniel's vision of the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven and receiving glory and kingdom – background for Jesus' words about the coming of the Son of Man in glory.
The Son of Man comes in his glory with all the angels – fulfillment of the promise of the glorious coming of the Son of Man.
Paul prays that hearts may be strengthened to stand blameless in holiness before God our Father when the Lord Jesus comes with all his holy ones.
Enoch prophesied that the Lord will come with his ten thousands of holy ones to execute judgment – the coming of the Son of Man with the holy ones.
Peter urges holding fast to the words spoken by the holy prophets and the command of the Lord – not being ashamed of the Lord's words.
